description: CrisisWatch Global is a solo engineering project by 11-year-old developer Shashwath S. based in Bengaluru, India. Our mission is to bridge the gap between orbital Earth-observation satellites and real-time humanitarian emergency response—turning complex space telemetry into an actionable 2D and 3D planetary crisis command center.
summary:
CrisisWatch Global is an interactive Earth-system trend and anomaly detection platform built by solo developer Shashwath S. (Team Coding Verse) to transform raw multi-agency satellite telemetry into clear planetary intelligence. Every day, Earth-observation satellites capture vast amounts of data on wildfires, severe storms, volcanic eruptions, sea-ice shifts, and seismic activity, yet these streams are often scattered across technical portals.

CrisisWatch unifies live global event feeds from NASA’s Earth Observatory Natural Event Tracker (EONET v3) and USGS seismic sensors onto a synchronized 2D Tactical Map and 3D Orbital Globe. Simultaneously, it computes real-time SGP4 orbital positions for eight international Earth-observation spacecraft—including NASA’s Terra, Aqua, Landsat 9, and Suomi NPP alongside ISS, ESA’s Sentinel-2A, ISRO’s Cartosat-3, and NOAA-20—showing how orbital sensors monitor unfolding surface anomalies. Powered by Google Gemini AI, CrisisWatch provides instant natural-language trend briefings and voice-assisted exploration, helping students, researchers, and citizens detect emerging environmental patterns at a glance.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

CrisisWatch Global is an interactive Earth System Trend Detective platform that unifies live planetary disaster telemetry, real-time multi-agency orbital satellite tracking, and conversational AI into a single command center. Users can toggle between a 2D Tactical Map and a 3D Orbital Globe to inspect active global environmental anomalies—including wildfires, severe storms, volcanic eruptions, sea-ice shifts, and earthquakes—as they unfold across the planet.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

Raw Earth-observation feeds from space agencies are often scattered across technical portals, making it difficult for students, citizens, and community responders to spot emerging environmental patterns quickly. CrisisWatch makes NASA and international Earth science immediately visual, understandable, and actionable for anyone worldwide.

Tools, Coding Languages & Data Used:

- Frontend & Architecture: Built with React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and interactive SVG/3D globe visualizations in Google AI Studio.

- Live Planetary Telemetry: Integrates NASA’s Earth Observatory Natural Event Tracker (EONET v3 API) for active wildfires, cyclones, floods, and volcanoes, alongside USGS Earthquake GeoJSON feeds for real-time seismic activity.

- Real-Time Orbital Mechanics: Uses satellite.js (SGP4 orbital propagation) and CelesTrak orbital elements to compute live second-by-second coordinates, altitudes, and velocities for eight international Earth-observation spacecraft—including NASA’s Terra, Aqua, Landsat 9, and Suomi NPP, the International Space Station (ISS), ESA’s Sentinel-2A, ISRO’s Cartosat-3, and NOAA-20.

- AI Trend Intelligence: Powered by Google Gemini AI (AEGIS-7) with Web Speech API voice interaction to summarize emerging climate anomalies and answer natural-language questions about active Earth systems.

Creativity & Design Considerations:

CrisisWatch combines live orbital physics with customizable tactical markers (Map Pin, Reticle, and Beacon styles), spatial anti-clutter clustering, and live aviation/maritime overlays—ensuring zero NASA branding alterations while delivering an engaging, accessible Earth-observation experience.
